title: ICE Is Running One of the Largest Anti-Left Surveillance Operations in US History
gist: Discovery in the 'Minnesota 15' case reveals HSI/ICE ran a vast undercover and data-fused surveillance campaign (about 120 agents, 15 TB of Signal chats, commercial data brokers, Patriot Act tools) against anti-ICE activists, which critics compare to COINTELPRO.

insights.claim: About 119-120 HSI agents, including 11 undercovers, worked the Minnesota 15 case, versus a peak of 42 CIA officers in the Vietnam-era MH/Chaos operation against the New Left.
insights.speaker: Ali Winston
insights.so_what: Scale is unprecedented for domestic dissent investigations, suggesting heavy DHS budget deployment.
insights.locator: Court records show 119 HSI agents worked

insights.claim: The case is funded through Operation Keyhole, an HSI certified undercover operation since 2008 that has funded at least 77 investigations and, as of June 2026, six active ones including Project Whipple Shield.
insights.speaker: Ali Winston
insights.so_what: Existing criminal-investigation funding was repurposed for political-adjacent targets.
insights.locator: Operation Keyhole is a long-standing program

insights.claim: National Security Presidential Memorandum 7, issued after Charlie Kirk's assassination, directs federal law enforcement to use every tool against groups that criticize the administration or espouse 'anti-Christian' ideas.
insights.speaker: Ali Winston
insights.so_what: A policy basis for broadened domestic investigations; legal challenges likely.

insights.claim: Agents used CBP Reaper drones, Patriot Act tools, the Treasury 314(a) program (29 subjects queried March 31, 2026), and 15 terabytes of infiltrated Signal chats.
insights.speaker: Ali Winston
insights.so_what: Counter-terror financial tools applied to activists will draw litigation and legislative scrutiny.

insights.claim: HSI tied a license-plate tool hosted on Fly.io to a person using DNS queries, Stripe data, commercial broker data, Minnesota DVS records, and Thomson-Reuters CLEAR to obtain SSN summaries, addresses and vehicles.
insights.speaker: Ali Winston
insights.so_what: Shows how cloud, payments and data-broker metadata deanonymize users; platforms face subpoena exposure.
insights.locator: After a local activist uploaded a license-plate search tool

insights.claim: Investigators used customs-and-taxation administrative summonses instead of warrants or grand jury subpoenas to obtain journalists' phone records, for conduct unrelated to customs.
insights.speaker: Ali Winston
insights.so_what: Legal workarounds may be struck down, creating press-freedom litigation risk.
insights.locator: HSI investigators used similar workarounds to warrants

insights.claim: Undercovers infiltrated trainings, marches, general strikes, church gatherings (apparently violating a court order) and Signal groups; conferences in Seattle, Michigan, Chicago and New York were surveilled.
insights.speaker: Ali Winston
insights.so_what: Encrypted-app trust depends on membership vetting; infiltration defeats encryption.
insights.locator: At least 11 undercover agents working under Operation Keyhole

insights.claim: Mike German says the key difference from past suppression of movements is the vast pool of available data, with broad monitoring used to link ever more people as potential subjects.
insights.speaker: Ali Winston
insights.so_what: Data availability, not new law, drives expanding surveillance capacity; data brokers benefit.
insights.quote: Broad monitoring of social media, communications, and financial transactions are used to link an ever increasing number of people
insights.locator: Mike German, a retired FBI agent

insights.claim: Defense attorney Kevin Riach says HSI is taking the FBI's place as 'investigative secret police' and calls the case the 'new COINTELPRO'.
insights.speaker: Ali Winston
insights.so_what: Expect court rulings on discovery and constitutionality to set precedent.

insights.claim: Former DHS counterterrorism lawyer Spencer Reynolds says the operation is not limited to Minnesota and runs in parallel to street-level raids led by Greg Bovino.
insights.speaker: Ali Winston
insights.so_what: Implies a nationwide intelligence apparatus supporting enforcement surges.
insights.locator: This operation does not seem in any way limited to Minnesota
